text:
Jules: FYI — EdgeChip asked to run a joint perf/W + sustained-throughput bench next month, wants kernel-level tuning included. thinking we coordinate a 2-week lab window and a short joint blog/marketplace blurb after results.
Ravi: +1. Do we have a specific model and sequence lengths they care about? perf/W varies a lot by seq len.
EdgeChipPM: Thanks! primary target is a 2B dense decoder workload (chat inference), 2–8 tokens/window, and a long-form throughput run at 2048 for tail latency. energy budget and rack PDU telemetry available.
Lena: Can we pin the model to gpt-small-like config for parity? also need to agree on quantization targets (fp16 vs int8).
Kai: I'd push a baseline fp16 run, then INT8 per-operator tune. Kernel patches we suggest: fused rotary + attention kernel reorder (small perf win but much better watt).
Jules: Sounds good. Let's define the metric set: 1) median p99 latency; 2) sustained throughput (tokens/s) at 95th percentile power; 3) joules/token; 4) perf/W curve over load sweep. Any additions?
Ravi: add KV-cache warm vs cold comparison and a small-horizon prefix-cache ablation. That's crucial for our runtime caching claims.
EdgeChipPM: We can provide power telemetry at 1s granularity and per-socket current. We'll also share firmware baseline and kernel build env. Need a signed NDA before we share full board images.
Lena: We'll need a reproducible harness. Proposal: use perf-harness v2 (our internal runner) with a config file like: 
```
model: rdl-gpt-small
precision: fp16
batch_sizes: [1,2,4,8]
sequence_lengths: [8,128,512,2048]
run_duration_s: 300
telemetry: /mnt/telemetry/pdu.csv
```
Make sure that runner exports per-step power and token timestamps.
Kai: For kernel tuning, let's keep patches in a branch 'edgechip-kernels-2026' and record git SHAs. We'll run before/after microbenchmarks: matmul, attention, KV load.
Jules: Timeline suggestion: week 1 dry run on our lab (sanity + infra); week 2 full sweep with EdgeChip present (remote or in-person). Deliverables: raw logs, cleaned perf tables, 3-page results summary, and a draft joint announcement.
EdgeChipPM: We can do in-person for week 2. We prefer Redwood to lead the writeup; we'll add an OEM section and marketplace listing blurb. Also coordinate legal on embargo (we need 72h review).
Ravi: Ops ask — which lab machines do we need? recommend 2x identical nodes per config (control vs tuned) to reduce noise. Also need a dedicated network vlan to avoid noisy neighbors.
Lena: I'll request 4 nodes from eng-infra: 2 baseline, 2 with kernel patches. Also opening a ticket for power-capture storage (bench-bot: allocate /bench/edgechip/2026).
bench-bot: bench-bot: created storage folder /bench/edgechip/2026 and set ACLs for Jules,Ravi,Lena,Kai,EdgeChipPM.
Kai: For reproducibility, let's commit Dockerfile + kernel build script to a temporary repo and share a snapshot tar with EdgeChip once NDA is signed.
Jules: Action items: Lena -> infra ticket + node reservation; Kai -> branch + build script; Ravi -> bench config + eval suites; EdgeChipPM -> NDA + firmware images. Target kickoff next Monday.
EdgeChipPM: NDA sent via email to legal@redwood.com, firmware drop scheduled upon NDA ack. Looking forward. :rocket:
Jules: Great. I'll post a short runbook in the partnerships drive and ping eng-platform for tracing hooks. Meeting to finalize timeline Monday 10am PT.
Ravi: I'll draft the results template (CSV columns + plotting scripts) and share before EOD Friday.
Lena: Nice. tagging @eng-infra and @legal in the runbook.
Kai: One small note — if we see thermal throttling at 2048, we should capture per-core frequency traces. add that to the runner collection.
EdgeChipPM: Noted. We'll bring a thermal probe as backup.
Jules: thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source of truth for scheduling/decisions. I'll update participants as needed.
